A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnyUp: Universal Feature Upsampling. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, depth, surface-normal, feature-generalization, and ablation experiments in Section 5, with additional qualitative results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds multi-backbone training, filter-basis sensitivity, computational profiling, and an implicit-FeatUp comparison.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1 explicitly describes extending attention computation with optional chunking to trade memory for speed and accommodate larger inputs. This is a limited execution-procedure extension; the feature-agnostic architecture, window attention, crop supervision, and losses in Equations (1)-(3) remain unchanged.

E1.justification: ImageNet training and the COCO-Stuff, PASCAL VOC, ADE20k, and NYUv2 evaluation coverage are retained. Additional backbone configurations, including DeiT, and lower-resolution evaluation remain within the existing feature-upsampling and downstream tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds FeatUp's implicit upsampling variant to the pretrained-probe comparison in Appendix B.2, Table 11. v1 evaluated FeatUp's joint bilateral upsampling variant. The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the experimental design with five-backbone training, a filter-basis-size sweep, and runtime/FLOPs/forward-backward-memory profiling at three resolutions on an A100. Table 11 introduces a separate 224px pretrained-probe comparison to accommodate implicit FeatUp; it does not replace the retained 448px experiment. Existing training budgets and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether mixed-backbone training improves unseen-encoder generalization, how filter-basis size affects quality, and how computational costs vary with resolution. These materially extend the investigation of generalization, component capacity, and efficiency. The original component-removal ablation and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2-6 and the original ablation table retain their scores, but v2 adds substantial result sets in Tables 7 and 9-11. For example, new Table 7 reports DeiT mIoU of 53.93 with DINOv2-only training versus 54.83 with multi-backbone training; Table 11 reports 37.91 for AnyUp versus 36.70 for implicit FeatUp at 224px. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds an analytical operation-count comparison: global attention requires H×W×h×w computations, while relative window size σ reduces this to H×W×σh×σw. Existing mathematical definitions and loss equations are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of encoder-agnostic, arbitrary-resolution upsampling, strong downstream performance, and feature-space preservation. The conclusion's added 'first-of-its-kind' wording repeats novelty already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the small DINOv2 degradation under mixed-backbone training to encoder-specific positional-artifact overfitting and interprets the basis sweep as evidence for distinguishing similarly colored regions through feature semantics. The original limitations remain. Its new blanket claim of over 50% runtime and memory savings is broader than Table 10 supports.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the chosen basis size M=128, relative window size σ=0.2, NATTEN implementation, A100 profiling hardware, and attention chunking. These supplement the retained optimizer, training budget, H100 training-time disclosure, and code/weight access statements; they do not establish changes to the original training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hassani et al. for the NATTEN implementation. It also replaces Siméoni et al.'s DINOv3 reference with Xue et al.'s DINOv3-UNet while continuing to discuss DINOv3 encoders, an apparent attribution error involving a different work. Most other reference edits are bibliographic updates, and the main research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization remain intact. v2 adds experimental paragraphs and an Additional Experiments appendix, shifts subsequent appendix letters, makes small terminology and grammar edits, and updates publication headers and bibliography formatting.

P2.justification: Quantitative presentation expands through four new tables covering mixed-backbone training, basis-size sensitivity, a two-panel computational profile, and implicit FeatUp. Figure 6 and Table 6 are relocated, and Figure 4's spatial labels change from H×W to h×w. Existing qualitative figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added controlled analyses, implicit-FeatUp comparison, computational measurements, and implementation details strengthen support for the retained method. However, the efficiency summary overstates Table 10: at 448px, 92.4 ms versus JAFAR's 113.9 ms is only an 18.9% reduction. The mismatched DINOv3 citation also reduces attribution accuracy. These issues temper an otherwise useful, limited overall improvement.
